rows.title_full: AN ACT RATIONALIZING THE NUMBERS OF HOLIDAYS IN THE PHILIPPINES, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE SECTION 26, CHAPTER 7, BOOK I OF EXECUTIVE ORDER NO. 292, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE ADMINISTRATIVE CODE OF 1987, AS AMENDED
rows.abstract:
Seeks to reduce the number of holidays to 12 days per year which is in line with the global median:  the eight traditional holidays such as:
New Year´s Day, Maundy Thursday, Good Friday, Black Saturday, Labor Day, Independence Day, All Saints´ Day, and Christmas Day; one holiday to commemorate all heroes on Rizal Day; one inter-faith/cultural holiday based on employees´ religious or cultural preferences; one holiday for both Ninoy Aquino´s death and People Power Revolution anniversaries;  one local holiday which shall fall on a Monday.
Proposes to move holidays to Mondays as much as possible to spur tourism and holiday spending to improve competitiveness and overall productivity.

rows.title_full: AN ACT ABOLISHING PHILIPPINE INTERNATIONAL TRADING CORPORATION (PITC), AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract:
Seeks to address the issues that the trade liberalization thrust of the global economy has made the mandate of the PITC redundant and irrelevant in the current times, and the passage of R.A. No.9184 (Government Procurement Reform Act) has also weakened the mandate of the PITC.
Tasks the DTI to undertake the functions of PITC related to facilitative trade-related services, responsive business solutions, and trade-related government-to-government transactions, among others.

Seeks to address the many issues and controversies surrounding the PS-DBM, most recent is in connection with the procurement of face shields, face masks, PPEs, and other pandemic-related purchases.
Proposes that the respective Departments, Agencies, Government-Owned and/or-Controlled Corporations (GOCCs), State Universities and Colleges, and Local Government Units shall take charge of the procurement of their common-use supplies, materials, and equipment.

Mandates all health care providers and health-related entities to comply with data standards to allow interoperability and health information exchange.

AN ACT IMPOSING A `SUPER-RICH TAX´ ON INDIVIDUALS WITH NET VALUE ASSETS EXCEEDING ONE BILLION PESOS (P1,000,000,000.00), AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE CERTAIN PROVISIONS OF THE NATIONAL INTERNAL REVENUE
21 CODE OF 1997 OR REPUBLIC ACT 10963 AS AMENDED
rows.abstract:
Defines SUPER-RICH TAX as the net value of taxable assets or the market value of assets owned by a taxpayer, real or personal, tangible or intangible, wherever situated, reduced by any debts owed by the taxpayer.
Proposes a tax on the super-rich Filipinos:
1% on wealth above Php1 billion, 2% on wealth above Php2 billion, and 3% on wealth over Php3 billion.
Proposes to aid the government in pursuing its anti-poverty measures and other social programs that can help stop the widening divide between the rich and the poor and help shift the burden of taxation away from regressive consumption taxes.

rows.title_full: AN ACT STRENGTHENING THE COMMISSION ON HIGHER EDUCATION AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE REPUBLIC ACT NO. 7722, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE “HIGHER EDUCATION ACT OF 1994”
rows.title_short: Amended Higher Education Act
rows.abstract:
Aims to modernize the Philippine higher education to keep pace with all the international and regional advancements.

States that the Commission on Higher Education (CHED) is independent and separate from the Department of Education (DepEd) and is attached to the Office of the President for administrative purposes only which shall cover both public and private HEIs offering degree programs, except those explicitly removed by Congress from its jurisdiction.

States that the Higher Development Fund established under Republic Act No. 7722 shall be used exclusively for the strengthening of higher education in all regions of the country.

Guarantees academic freedom of universities and colleges and religious freedom of higher education student, faculty, or other members of the academic community; Enumerates the powers and functions as well as the quasi-judicial powers of the CHED, among others.
